title: Taxi Driver Claims Hotel is Closed, Burned, or in a Riot Zone
answer: This is one of the most common scams in Delhi, Mumbai, and Agra. The driver wants a massive commission from an overpriced budget hotel. Never believe a driver who says your hotel is closed, demolished, or inaccessible due to a festival. Insist firmly: 'Please take me to my hotel address anyway.' Call your hotel's official phone number directly. If the driver refuses, demand to be dropped at the nearest police station or metro station.
sourceLabel: Ministry of Tourism & Delhi Police Travel Advisory

title: Auto-Rickshaw Fare & Meter Refusal
answer: In most Indian cities (Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru), auto drivers are legally required to use the electronic meter. If a driver refuses and quotes 3x the normal rate, say: 'Meter se chaliye' (Please go by meter). Alternatively, use app-based booking like Uber, Ola, or Rapido where the fare is fixed and tracked by GPS. Pre-paid taxi/auto booths at airports and major railway stations are safe and regulated.

title: Indian e-Visa Arrival Checklist & Permitted Ports
answer: Foreign tourists must carry a physical printed copy of the electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) confirmation email. Your passport must have at least 6 months validity from the date of arrival and at least 2 blank pages. e-Visa is valid for entry at 31 designated international airports (Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata, Bengaluru, Goa, etc.) and 5 designated seaports. Biometrics (fingerprints and photo) will be captured at immigration.
sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration Official e-Visa Portal

title: FRRO Registration: When is it Mandatory?
answer: Foreign tourists holding an e-Tourist Visa valid for continuous stay of up to 180 days do NOT need to register with the FRRO unless their continuous stay exceeds 180 days or an explicit endorsement is stamped on their visa. All foreign nationals must ensure their hotel submits a 'Form C' on check-in. If you change address or overstay due to medical emergency, you must apply online on the e-FRRO portal within 14 days.
sourceLabel: Ministry of Home Affairs e-FRRO Portal

title: Drinking Water & Avoiding Delhi Belly
answer: Never drink unfiltered tap water in India. Always drink bottled mineral water from reputable brands (Bisleri, Aquafina, Kinley) and check that the plastic seal is unbroken. Avoid ice cubes in roadside stalls, raw unpeeled salads, and cut fruits sitting in open air. Eat at crowded street stalls where hot food is cooked fresh before your eyes. Carry Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS) and activated charcoal or loperamide.
sourceLabel: CDC & WHO Travelers Health Guidelines for India

title: Buying an Indian SIM Card as a Foreign Tourist
answer: You can purchase a tourist SIM card directly at international arrival halls (Airtel or Jio kiosk) at major airports. You will need your physical passport, valid Indian visa, passport photo, and your hotel address in India. Verification takes 2 to 4 hours, after which you dial 59059 to tele-verify. Alternatively, buy an international e-SIM (Airalo, Nomad) before flying, but note that Indian UPI apps generally require a local Indian (+91) phone number.

title: The Fake New Delhi Railway Station Tourist Bureau Scam
answer: Touts standing outside New Delhi Railway Station (Paharganj side) will tell you that the International Tourist Bureau has moved, is closed, or that all trains are cancelled due to track repair. They will lead you to a private travel agency in Connaught Place that charges thousands of dollars for fake private car packages. The REAL International Tourist Bureau is located on the 1st Floor of New Delhi Railway Station. Official train bookings are only done on irctc.co.in.

title: Paying in India: Cash, Cards & Tourist UPI
answer: Cash (Indian Rupees / INR) is still essential for small auto rides, fruit sellers, and temple offerings. ATMs are widely available, but inform your bank of travel to prevent card blocks. The Reserve Bank of India has launched 'UPI One World' for foreign tourists, allowing you to use UPI mobile scan-to-pay via prepaid wallets issued at select airport foreign exchange counters.
sourceLabel: Reserve Bank of India UPI for Foreign Inbound Travelers

title: Temple & Mosque Etiquette: Shoes, Clothes & Cameras
answer: Always remove your shoes and socks before entering Hindu temples, Jain temples, and mosques. Dedicated shoe stands are available at the entrance (tip ₹10-20 upon collection). Dress modestly with shoulders and knees covered. At Sikh Gurudwaras, wash your feet at the entrance basin and cover your head with a scarf or bandana. Photography is usually strictly forbidden inside the inner sanctum.

title: Emergency Numbers in India: Police, Ambulance & Fire
answer: 112 is the single unified Emergency Response Support System (ERSS) across India, equivalent to 911 or 112 in Europe. Dialing 112 connects you to Police, Ambulance, and Fire services with English-speaking dispatchers. For specific tourist police inquiries, you can also dial 1363 (Incredible India Tourist Helpline, available 24/7 in 12 languages including English, German, French, and Spanish).
sourceLabel: Emergency Response Support System (ERSS) Ministry of Home Affairs
